statement: For the free profinite product C2 amalg C3, preservation of the conjugacy classes of its finite factors does not imply preservation of the cusp subgroup generated by their product. A fully checked PSL2(F13) quotient gives a counterexample lifted to an actual profinite automorphism. The corrected finite-factor automorphism lifting theorem for every profinite quotient is derived completely from Efrat's Main Theorem, compactness and Hopficity.
manuscript_passages: Section47; folios416-420 verso; cote140-3 scans231-240; further attack on the prescribed relative action in PartB afterLM2(4)
notes: The two marked pairs generate PSL2(F13), order1092, and have conjugate factors of orders2,3, but products of orders13 and7. Efrat's theorem lifts these to factor-preserving profinite automorphisms; it does not preserve the cusp or the normalized section47 equation. This is a rigorous failed-shortcut test, not a full profinite q7 lift.
